about.title: About and data notice
about.data1: Sensor models are calibrated from open research datasets and published specifications; all scenarios are authored or procedurally generated.
about.data2: No real operational or classified data is used. No claim of validated training effectiveness or doctrine accuracy is made; any effectiveness result will come only from our own measured pilot.
about.scope1: Defensive training only: recognise, classify, respond. The platform contains no instructions for building, arming or operating attack drones and no real-world targeting detail.
about.scope2: Rules of engagement are a fictional, editable rule set.
about.affiliation: This is an independent student project. It has no official affiliation with the Ministry of Defence, the Defence Services Staff College, DRDO, the Indian armed forces or any government programme.

hard-fail.no-positive-id: Engaged track {{track}} at {{t}} without a positive ID (classified, and assessed hostile or suspect). The contact fails: score 0.

finding.blocked-attempt: The rules blocked {{attempts}} of your responses on this contact.
finding.false-alarm: Clutter classified as {{given}}. The contact was {{actual}}.
finding.false-engagement: Engaged track {{track}} at {{t}}, which followed nothing real.
finding.not-presented: No sensor reported this contact during the session, so it was not scored.
finding.not-worked: A sensor reported this contact and no action was taken on it. Leaving it alone was correct, so it was not scored.

detect.band: {{threat}}: act sooner. Your first action came {{seconds}} after the first sensor report; the standard is {{standard}}. Designate or classify a track as soon as it appears.
detect.missed: {{threat}}: no action was taken. Designate and classify every contact within {{standard}} of its first sensor report.

classify.correct: {{threat}}: classify sooner. The class was right but took {{seconds}} against a standard of {{standard}}. Cue the EO sensor onto the track to confirm the class earlier.
classify.wrong: {{threat}}: you called it {{given}} and it was {{actual}}. Cue the EO sensor and check size, rotors and wings before you commit.
classify.unknown: {{threat}}: you left the class as unknown and it was {{actual}}. Commit to the best-supported class once EO or IR has a view.
classify.missing: {{threat}}: no class was set. Classify every contact you work.

assess.partial: {{threat}}: assessing it as {{given}} earned partial credit for a {{actual}} contact. Weigh class, behaviour and zone before you settle on an identity.
assess.wrong: {{threat}}: you assessed it as {{given}} and it was {{actual}}. Check the class and the filed flights before you set an identity.
assess.missing: {{threat}}: no assessment was made. Assess every contact you work.

respond.engage-higher: {{threat}}: you used {{effector}}, above the first effector the rule lists. Use the lowest escalation the rule permits.
respond.report-only: {{threat}}: you reported but did not engage. When a rule permits a response on a hostile contact, take it in time.
respond.hold-only: {{threat}}: you only held fire on a hostile contact. Read the rule preview to find the response it permits, and apply it in time.
respond.none: {{threat}}: no response was made on a hostile contact. Open Respond (R) on every hostile contact.
respond.engage: {{threat}}: respond sooner. The response took {{seconds}} against a standard of {{standard}}, and blocked attempts cost marks.

report.missing: {{threat}}: no contact report was filed. File class, position, count, heading and confidence for every hostile contact.
report.filed: {{threat}}: your weakest report field was {{worst_field}}. Check it against the track table before filing, and file within {{standard}} of the first sensor report.

hard-fail.engaged-non-hostile: {{threat}}: you engaged a contact that was {{actual}}. Never engage before the contact is identified as hostile.
hard-fail.no-positive-id: {{threat}}: you engaged without a positive ID. Classify the track and assess it hostile or suspect before any engagement.

lesson.track-error: {{threat}}: a track error at {{t}} was left uncorrected. After a swap, split or merge, check the labels and restore them.
lesson.blocked-attempt: {{threat}}: the rules blocked {{attempts}} of your responses. Read the rule preview before you commit a response.
lesson.false-engagement: Track {{track}} followed nothing real and was engaged at {{t}}. Confirm a track on a second sensor before you engage it.

extra.changes: Class calls changed before the final one: {{changes}}.
extra.blocked: Responses blocked by the rules on this contact: {{blocked_attempts}}.

debrief.reference: Reference scoring: timing standards and weights are fictional and editable. The score measures what was done against this scenario's rules. It is not validated as a measure of operator skill.

summary.criterionNote: The form of c is the standard one and has not been checked against a primary source.

bench.title: Render benchmark
bench.done: Finished. Download the JSON and record it in docs/PERFORMANCE.md.
bench.canvas: Benchmark scene preview, drawn at 1920 by 1080 pixels
bench.emptyBody: Runs the reference scene (rural terrain pack, 24-drone placeholder swarm, 30 birds, thermal pass) at 1920 × 1080 for each graphics tier and for Auto, about two minutes in all. Keep this tab in front and close other applications.
bench.noWebgl: WebGL is not available in this browser, so the benchmark cannot run.
bench.gateBody: Passes if the High tier holds a median of 45 fps or more with the 5th percentile at 30 fps or more, or if Auto holds a median and a 5th percentile of 30 fps or more. Figures are for this machine only.
bench.fixedHigh: High tier, thermal: median ≥ 45 fps and 5th percentile ≥ 30 fps
bench.autoHolds: Auto tier: median and 5th percentile ≥ 30 fps
bench.notes: Thermal is a rendering model, not radiometric. The swarm and birds are placeholder markers. Frame times are display-refresh intervals, so a 60 Hz screen caps results at 60 fps.
